questions.question: Motorcyclists should avoid riding on the oily strip in the center of a traffic lane. Why?

options.text: Oil and grease reduce tire grip.
There is no need to worry about oil and grease.
Find a lane with less oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oil and grease reduce tire grip.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease. The oily strip is usually only about two feet wide. You can ride to the left or right side of it and still stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: What should you do with the front brake when making a U-turn?

options.text: Use both front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake. It could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake. It could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip over. Use only the rear brake to slow down during the U-turn.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic. This keeps you away from the passing driver and reduces danger for both of you.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what is the best place to ride?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you instead of the center of the lane. The left tire track is often best, but this can change based on traffic.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time?

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is the best way.
Just start riding. Most bikes are similar, so no preparation is needed.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Each bike is different. Before riding, check the bike's safety and maintenance. Find where everything is located. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to understand how the bike operates.

questions.question: Why should you change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To prevent a sudden change in engine power during the turn.
So both hands stay on the handlebars during the turn.
To keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent a sudden change in engine power during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before turning to avoid sudden power changes while leaning. Shifting during a turn can cause the rear wheel to skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What causes an engine to seize?
questions.correctAnswerText: Not enough oil.
questions.explanation: An engine seizes when oil is too low. Without oil, engine parts cannot move smoothly and the engine overheats and stops working.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, during a crash. A windshield is not a good replacement.

questions.question: What separates traffic lanes moving in the same direction?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean no passing. Dashed lines mean passing is allowed if it is safe.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, where should you ride?

options.text: On the right side of the lane.
On the edge of the road.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, the road becomes very slippery. Rainwater mixes with oil left by cars on the road. Riding in tire tracks helps you avoid the slippery oil on the pavement.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT significantly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role in determining BAC.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers should always sit behind the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist or hips. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never sit sidesaddle.

questions.question: How do you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: The only way to become sober is to give your body time to process the alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle could block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What kind of gloves should you wear when riding a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Full-fingered gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Choose gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help you maintain control when turning a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To maintain control in a turn, slow down before entering it. Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Press the handlebar to lean the right direction. Gently roll on the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: What should you wear while riding to protect your hearing?

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a full-face helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: What about the oily strip down the center of a lane?

options.text: Ride on it only if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
It provides good traction unless it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: It provides good traction unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is usually oily but provides enough traction for safe riding when dry. In rain, avoid it. The oily strip is typically about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What should riders know about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders should check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular riding routine.
